# SK0209 — The expression parentheses are not arranged

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

`skala arrange` would remove redundant parentheses.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Formatting |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Syntax |
| Needs a compilation | no |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

Parenthesis removal is the arranger's highest-risk syntactic cleanup, so each removal is proved rather than computed: the parentheses go only when the expression printed without them parses back to the same tree. Which redundant parentheses Skala is willing to lose is a separate, configured question — `skala_parentheses_redundancy_style` and the three `dotnet_style_parentheses_in_*_binary_operators` keys decide it. It runs by default; there is no opt-in flag.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
return (value);
```

Write:

```csharp
return value;
```

## When it does not fire

None relative to the effective configuration: a removal that would change the parse is refused by construction. At the default `remove_if_not_clarifies_precedence`, parentheses the configuration keeps for clarity remain — around the operands of shift and bitwise operators, and around a nested `&&`, `||` or `??` under `always_for_clarity`; `remove` takes those too, as the oracle does. At either value so do parentheses after a cast-shaped `(A)(b)`, parentheses with a preprocessor directive inside them, and two shapes the parse alone allows and the oracle keeps: a `switch` expression as the receiver of `with` or the subject of another `switch`, and a `switch` or binary operand of a `throw` expression. ⚠ Assignments, conditionals, lambdas, queries and `switch` expressions used to be kept whole, and interpolation holes declined whole, on the belief that the oracle leaves them alone; measured, it removes them wherever the parse allows (#392), so the proof decides them now and re-parses the interpolated string, the argument list or the `switch` arm a removal sits in rather than the parenthesised expression alone. A comment inside the parentheses is carried out with the expression. Formatter-off regions are excluded. To keep every parenthesis, exclude the rule with `skala arrange --exclude SK0209`.

## Configuration

- `skala_parentheses_redundancy_style`
- `dotnet_style_parentheses_in_arithmetic_binary_operators`
- `dotnet_style_parentheses_in_relational_binary_operators`
- `dotnet_style_parentheses_in_other_binary_operators`
